clue.text: Bit of slap and tickle starts to arouse my suspicions about artist

indicators.note: to tickle is to stir or agitate, so the picked initials are jostled into a new order
the starts of the three words that follow are taken, their opening letters only

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
RA is a Royal Academician, the stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone's bit of slap and tickle makes them suspicious of an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap and tickle' reads as one phrase for canoodling, but 'slap' is British slang for make-up and 'tickle' is the anagram signal: the initials A, M, S become MAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is British slang for cosmetics, and eyelash colouring is one item of make-up.

clue.text: Very small, quiet nursing home

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the word for quiet holds the word for home

parts.note: mute means silent, quiet
in means at home

explanation.surface: A small, peaceful care home.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny, minuscule: a synonym for extremely small.

clue.text: English dons get lost and cry

indicators.note: to don is to put on, as clothing; the letter is wrapped in the word for get lost

parts.note: scram means go away, get lost

explanation.surface: English university lecturers lose their way and weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like Oxbridge lecturers; it is a verb meaning wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek or yell is a loud cry.

clue.text: I mess about, struggling to be self-disciplined

indicators.note: struggling means flailing and in disorder, so the letters of I mess about are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone admits to fooling around while trying to stay disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like an anagram signal; it is part of the fodder, and 'struggling' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious people practise self-denial, especially with food and drink.

clue.text: Reckless lighting of gas rings upset head of Npower

parts.note: Ar is the chemical symbol for argon, a gas

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: O is a ring shape, so rings are Os

indicators.note: the head of Npower is its first letter

explanation.surface: Carelessly lighting a gas hob unsettles the boss of a British energy supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: Npower is a British gas and electricity company.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fires is criminal fire-raising, a crime of reckless kindling.

clue.text: Battered tins of cake regularly disappearing off the shelf

indicators.note: something battered has been knocked out of shape, so the word tins is rearranged
every other letter of the words of cake vanishes, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Dented tins of cake keep vanishing from the supermarket shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' rearranges TINS as INST; 'regularly disappearing' drops F, A and E from OF CAKE, leaving OCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bought off the shelf are ready-made and available now, which is what a shop holding them has.

clue.text: Sailor, one from the Gulf, picked up a lover

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up raises the letters, reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
an Omani comes from Oman on the Persian Gulf

explanation.surface: A sailor and a man from the Gulf found a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a homophone signal; it reverses TAROMANI.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian-derived word for a woman who is loved, a female sweetheart.

clue.text: Father and husband leaving county

indicators.note: the husband leaves, so his letter is removed from the county

parts.note: a shire is a county

explanation.surface: A dad and husband moving out of the county.
explanation.definitionFit: A sire is a male parent, especially of an animal; to sire is to father.

clue.text: Not very proactive, dithering like Norma?

indicators.note: dithering is wavering confusedly, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not very means without the very, so its letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A hesitant, rather passive woman named Norma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops V from PROACTIVE; 'dithering' anagrams the rest. Norma is Bellini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a Bellini opera, so anything like it belongs to opera; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Art of teasing youngster over diary entry's conclusion

parts.note: a kid is a youngster
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a log is a diary or record

indicators.note: the conclusion of entry is its final letter

explanation.surface: A child mocks the last line of someone's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entry's' looks possessive; its conclusion is Y, last before the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychological games or bluffing to tease or wind someone up; British slang for kidding.

clue.text: Partially unmask rancidly repellent police spies

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
only part of the run of letters across unmask rancidly is used

explanation.surface: Unmasking rancid, repellent informers, a bit at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partially' takes SKRAN from the end of unmaSK and start of RANcidly; 'repellent' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is British slang for an informer who passes tips to the police.

clue.text: Vacuously self-important ass in top-flight location

indicators.note: the word self-important is emptied of its contents, keeping only its two ends

parts.note: an ass is a fool, as is an airhead

explanation.surface: An empty-headed, pompous fool occupies some lofty position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacuously' empties self-important to S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: The landing at the head of a stair is literally at the top of a flight of steps, a pun on top-flight meaning elite.

clue.text: Rudely intrude on a group of workers

indicators.note: done rudely, roughly and without care, so the letters of intrude on a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone barges in on a gathering of employees without asking.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour organisation is a body of employees banded together to bargain for pay and conditions.

clue.text: Clay (Muhammad Ali) routed Liston to begin with

indicators.note: each of the four words is used only for its beginning, its first letter

explanation.surface: Cassius Clay, later Muhammad Ali, beat Sonny Liston at the start of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clay' looks like the boxer's original name; it is the definition, the earthy material.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly lime-rich earth used as fertiliser is a kind of clay soil.

clue.text: Quitting position, adopting extremely uncivil language

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the word for position takes in the others

parts.note: to put is to position, to place

indicators.note: the extremes of uncivil are its first and last letters

parts.note: lingo is slang for language

explanation.surface: Leaving a post while using very rude speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing from an arrangement or an occupied place: quitting.

clue.text: Pretentious reporting of theft in Israeli port

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so the phrase is judged by how it is said

parts.note: Haifa is a port in Israel, and looting is theft

explanation.surface: A news report of a robbery in an Israeli harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose, pompous language or manners are pretentious in style.

clue.text: Dangerous quality of much air in Essex

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The perilous effect of strong winds in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dangerous quality' turns on 'hairy', slang for scary or risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is informal for frightening or risky, so its noun means riskiness.

clue.text: Last of ascetic and devout desert mystics seeing doctors

indicators.note: to desert is to abandon, so the picked letters abandon the word for mystics

parts.note: occultists are mystics who study hidden powers

indicators.note: the final letter of each of ascetic and devout

explanation.surface: Ascetics and devout desert hermits have visions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like sand; it is a verb: C and T, the 'Last of' ascetic and devout, leave OCCULTISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye specialists are doctors concerned with seeing and sight.

clue.text: Rude little devil runs after guy?

indicators.note: after puts the letter for runs behind the word for guy

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
a guy is a rope securing a tent
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cheeky child chases after some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man; it is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or unseemly behaviour is rude, not proper.

clue.text: Catching Tommy, Eunice bounds away into lead

indicators.note: the trimmed names go into the word for lead

parts.note: an electrical lead is a cable

indicators.note: the bounds of Tommy and Eunice, their outer letters, are taken away

explanation.surface: Tommy and Eunice escape the leash after being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching' looks like grabbing hold, but means infectious; 'bounds' are the names' outer letters, not leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A catching illness is infectious, one that can be passed from person to person.

clue.text: Allen losing everything in Sin City

indicators.note: the trimmed name goes in the word for sin

parts.note: vice is wickedness, sin

indicators.note: the name loses the letters of everything

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Woody Allen loses his shirt in Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sin City' looks like Las Vegas; 'Sin' gives VICE and 'City' is the definition. 'losing' takes ALL from ALLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian lagoon port is a famous city.

clue.text: Wise Olympian subsequently enters races alternately

indicators.note: the word for subsequently enters the letters picked from races
alternate letters of races are used

parts.note: then means afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: A clever Olympic athlete then takes part in races in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete; it means a god on Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom, one of the gods dwelling on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Tempt government to swap sides

indicators.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two sides, and these trade places

parts.note: to rule is to govern, and rule means government

explanation.surface: Luring the government into crossing the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swap sides' exchanges R (right) and L (left) within RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to tempt them with bait.

clue.text: Throw dance party close to Oban? Sure thing!

parts.note: a disco is a party for dancing

indicators.note: the close of Oban is its last letter

parts.note: a cert, short for certainty, is a sure thing

explanation.surface: Someone throws a dance party near a Scottish town and is sure it will go well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like hosting the party; it means unsettle. Oban is a Scottish west-coast town.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to unsettle or fluster them.

clue.text: Hybrid vehicle not a huge success at first

indicators.note: not a means without the letter A

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, huge

indicators.note: only the first letter of success

explanation.surface: A hybrid car that was a flop at launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid vehicle' reads as one phrase; only 'Hybrid' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross is a hybrid, the offspring of two different breeds or varieties.

clue.text: Small group of patriots

indicators.note: of shows the letters come out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A small band of loyal nationalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Three performers or people form a small group, a threesome.

clue.text: Perhaps Wonder Woman cured our herpes

indicators.note: cured meat is processed and changed, so the letters of our herpes are reworked

explanation.surface: A comic-book heroine has cleared up an embarrassing infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonder Woman is one example of a costumed comic-book crimefighter with special powers.

clue.text: Sheepish old climber

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: An embarrassed elderly mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like embarrassed; read literally it means of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, sheepish means relating to sheep, the meaning of the Latin-derived adjective.

clue.text: They offer trips and the ultimate in luxurious hotel accommodation

indicators.note: the ultimate letter, the last, of luxurious

parts.note: Hotel is the radio code word for the letter H
rooms are accommodation

explanation.surface: A travel agent's luxury hotels sell holiday trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' looks like holidays but means drug-induced hallucinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for hallucinogenic mushrooms, which give users psychedelic experiences.

clue.text: Cry of defiance from drunkard at this point

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
here means at this point

explanation.surface: A drunk shouts defiantly from where he stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish retort of triumph or defiance, said to close an argument.
